questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The epididymis primarily:
opts: Transports sperm to the vas deferens
Drains lymph to the inguinal nodes
questions.exp: The epididymis transports sperm to the vas deferens. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The seminiferous tubules are the site of:
questions.exp: Seminiferous tubules are the site of spermatogenesis. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The rete testis transports sperm to the:
questions.exp: The rete testis transports sperm to the epididymis. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: Accumulation of fluid in the tunica vaginalis produces:
questions.exp: Fluid accumulation in the tunica vaginalis causes a hydrocele. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The left testicular vein drains:
opts: At a right angle into the left renal vein
Directly into the inferior vena cava
questions.exp: The left testicular vein drains at a right angle into the left renal vein. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The longer course of the left testicular vein contributes to the fact that:
questions.exp: The left testicular vein has a longer course and left varicocele is more common. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The first lymphatic basin for the left testis is the:
questions.exp: Left testicular lymphatics drain first to the para-aortic group. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The first lymphatic basin for the right testis is the:
questions.exp: Right testicular lymphatics drain first to the interaortocaval group. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The testis develops in the:
questions.exp: The testis develops in the genital ridge, which is retroperitoneal. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: Which is a trigger for descent of the testis?
questions.exp: Triggers for descent include the pull of the contractile gubernaculum. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: The gubernaculum is described in the chapter as:
opts: A part of the tunica albuginea
questions.exp: The gubernaculum is contractile tissue involved in testicular descent. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
questions.q: Besides the gubernaculum, testicular descent is aided by:
opts: Hormonal factors and differential growth of the abdominal wall
Only closure of the inguinal canal
Only contraction of the dartos muscle
questions.exp: Hormonal factors and differential growth of the abdominal wall are also descent triggers. (Book p307)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: An undescended testis is one that:
opts: Is arrested along the normal path of descent
Has deviated from the normal path
Has undergone torsion in the scrotum
questions.exp: An undescended testis is arrested along its normal path of descent. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The most common site of arrest of an undescended testis is the:
questions.exp: The inguinal canal is the most common site of arrest. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Undescended testis is more common on the:
opts: Two sides equally in every case
questions.exp: Right-sided undescended testis is more common because the right testis descends later. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Bilateral undescended testes are termed:
questions.exp: Bilateral undescended testes are called cryptorchidism. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The testis begins its descent at approximately:
questions.exp: The timeline shows that testicular descent begins at 3 months of intrauterine life. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: At approximately 6 months of intrauterine life, the descending testis lies in the:
questions.exp: At 6 months the testis lies in the iliac fossa. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: At approximately 7 months of intrauterine life, the testis lies in the:
questions.exp: At 7 months the testis lies in the inguinal canal. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: At approximately 8 months of intrauterine life, the testis lies at the:
questions.exp: At 8 months the testis lies at the superficial ring. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The testis reaches the scrotum at approximately:
questions.exp: The timeline shows scrotal arrival at 9 months of intrauterine life. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: A characteristic change in an undescended testis is:
questions.exp: An undescended testis has decreased volume. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Undescended testis is associated with an increased risk of:
opts: Intratubular germ cell neoplasia and seminoma
questions.exp: Undescended testis increases intratubular germ cell neoplasia and seminoma risk. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: In an undescended testis, which cells are affected more?
questions.exp: Sertoli cells are affected more in an undescended testis. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The effect of undescended testis on Sertoli cells is:
questions.exp: Sertoli-cell injury causes reduced spermatogenesis. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Leydig cells in an undescended testis are affected less, so there are usually:
questions.exp: Leydig cells are affected less and secondary sexual characteristics remain normal. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The higher the undescended testis, the:
opts: Less the risk of histological change
questions.exp: Higher position is associated with more histological changes. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Which is a listed complication of an undescended testis?
questions.exp: Trauma is one of the listed complications of an undescended testis. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Sterility associated with an undescended testis is particularly described in:
questions.exp: Sterility is described in cryptorchidism; early surgery is recommended. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: If surgery for cryptorchidism is delayed until adulthood, the patient may:
questions.exp: When surgery is done in adulthood, infertility may persist. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The most common associated hernia in undescended testis is:
questions.exp: Indirect inguinal hernia is the commonest associated hernia, listed as about 95%. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The most common malignancy associated with undescended testis is:
questions.exp: Seminoma is the most common malignancy associated with an undescended testis. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Surgery for an undescended testis is recommended before puberty mainly to:
opts: Increase the length of the vas deferens
questions.exp: Surgery before puberty reduces the risk of cancer. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: An undescended testis is commonly reported by the:
questions.exp: Clinical presentation is commonly reported by the mother. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Absent scrotal rugosities suggest:
questions.exp: Scrotal rugosities are absent in the clinical presentation of an undescended testis. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: An inguinal undescended testis is usually:
questions.exp: An inguinal testis is palpable. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The investigation of choice for an inguinal undescended testis is:
questions.exp: Ultrasonography is used for an inguinal testis. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The investigation of choice for an intra-abdominal undescended testis is:
questions.exp: Diagnostic laparoscopy is the investigation of choice for an intra-abdominal testis. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Spontaneous descent of the testis can occur until approximately:
questions.exp: Spontaneous descent can occur until 5 months; conservative management is used until then. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The ideal timing of surgery for an undescended testis is:
questions.exp: The ideal timing of surgery is 6–12 months of age. (Book p308)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: In bilateral undescended testis, the initial protocol uses:
questions.exp: The bilateral cryptorchidism protocol begins with a single dose of beta-hCG. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: In bilateral undescended testes, no response to beta-hCG suggests:
questions.exp: No response to beta-hCG in the bilateral protocol suggests anorchia. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: In bilateral cryptorchidism, a rise in testosterone with raised FSH and LH is followed by:
questions.exp: Raised testosterone with FSH and LH leads to laparoscopy and exploration in the protocol. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: For a unilateral undescended testis, the initial operative evaluation is:
questions.exp: Laparoscopy is used in the unilateral undescended testis protocol. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: At laparoscopy, an intra-abdominal testis that is necrotic or rudimentary is managed by:
questions.exp: A necrotic or rudimentary intra-abdominal testis is treated by orchidectomy. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: At laparoscopy, a viable intra-abdominal testis is managed by:
questions.exp: A viable intra-abdominal testis is treated with orchidopexy. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: If the testicular vessels are seen exiting the deep ring, the next step is:
questions.exp: Vessels exiting the deep ring lead to inguinal exploration. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Blind-ending testicular vessels in the unilateral protocol suggest monorchia or:
questions.exp: Blind-ending vessels suggest monorchia or intrauterine torsion. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Blind-ending testicular vessels are managed by:
questions.exp: The remnant is excised when the vessels are blind-ending. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: Fowler–Stephens orchidopexy is a:
questions.exp: Fowler–Stephens orchidopexy is a two-stage procedure. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The first stage of Fowler–Stephens orchidopexy involves:
opts: High ligation of testicular vessels and mobilisation into the inguinal canal
questions.exp: Stage 1 is high ligation of testicular vessels plus mobilisation into the inguinal canal. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The rationale for high ligation in Fowler–Stephens orchidopexy is to create a:
opts: Longer pedicle that is easier to mobilise
Shorter pedicle with no blood supply
questions.exp: High ligation creates a longer pedicle that is easier to mobilise. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The second stage of Fowler–Stephens orchidopexy is performed after a few weeks and involves:
opts: Mobilisation of the testis into the scrotum
Closure of the processus vaginalis only
questions.exp: Stage 2 mobilises the testis into the scrotum after a few weeks. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The best method of orchidopexy listed in the chapter is:
questions.exp: Silbaar is listed as the best orchidopexy method. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: In the Silbaar method, the testicular vessels are cut and followed by:
opts: Microvascular anastomosis with branches of the internal iliac
questions.exp: Silbaar uses microvascular anastomosis with branches of the internal iliac after cutting the testicular vessels. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: An ectopic testis is one that:
opts: Deviates from the normal path of descent
Is arrested along the normal path
questions.exp: An ectopic testis deviates from the normal path of descent. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The most common site of an ectopic testis is the:
opts: Superficial inguinal pouch near the superficial ring
questions.exp: The superficial inguinal pouch close to the superficial ring is the commonest ectopic site. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The treatment of an ectopic testis is:
questions.exp: Ectopic testis is managed by orchidopexy. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: A retractile testis is considered a:
questions.exp: Retractile testis is a normal variant. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: A retractile testis may:
opts: Occasionally jump into the inguinal canal and return to the scrotum
questions.exp: A retractile testis can occasionally jump into the inguinal canal and return to the scrotum by itself or manual repositioning. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
questions.q: The management of a retractile testis is:
questions.exp: A retractile testis is managed with reassurance. (Book p309)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: The bell-clapper deformity predisposes to torsion because of:
opts: High attachment of the tunica vaginalis
Low attachment of the tunica vaginalis
questions.exp: Bell-clapper testis has high attachment of the tunica vaginalis. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: Which is a risk factor for testicular torsion?
opts: A descended testis with normal attachment only
questions.exp: Testicular inversion is a listed risk factor for torsion. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: An undescended testis is a risk factor for:
questions.exp: Undescended testis is a risk factor for testicular torsion. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: Separation of the testis from the epididymis is a:
questions.exp: A testis separating from the epididymis is a rare torsion risk factor. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: The typical patient with testicular torsion is a:
questions.exp: Testicular torsion typically affects a young male. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: The pain of testicular torsion is typically:
questions.exp: Torsion causes acute-onset severe scrotal pain. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: Acute swelling in a young male with severe scrotal pain should raise suspicion of:
questions.exp: Acute swelling accompanies the acute pain of torsion. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: In testicular torsion, lifting the testis on Prehn's sign causes:
opts: No change in pain in every case
questions.exp: The book contrasts torsion, in which lifting the testis increases pain, with epididymo-orchitis, in which pain decreases. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: In torsion, the affected testis lies:
opts: At the level of the knee
questions.exp: The Deming sign is a higher-riding testis on the side of torsion. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: A transversely placed testis is suggestive of:
questions.exp: A transverse lie is a listed sign of torsion. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: A 720-degree twist causes more rapid ischaemia than a twist of:
questions.exp: A 720-degree twist causes more rapid ischaemia than a twist of less than 360 degrees. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: If testicular torsion is untwisted within 6 hours, the chance of salvage is approximately:
questions.exp: Untwisting within 6 hours gives a 100% chance of salvage in the chapter. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: If testicular torsion is treated after 24 hours, the chance of salvage is approximately:
questions.exp: After more than 24 hours the listed chance of salvage is 20%. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: The diagnosis of testicular torsion is primarily:
questions.exp: Torsion is diagnosed clinically and supported by Doppler. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: Doppler in testicular torsion shows:
opts: Absent blood flow in the testis
A normal testicular flow in every case
questions.exp: Doppler shows absent blood flow in the affected testis. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: The operative management of suspected testicular torsion is:
questions.exp: Scrotal exploration is the operative management of torsion. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: At exploration, a viable torsed testis is managed by:
questions.exp: A viable testis is de-rotated and fixed by orchidopexy. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: At exploration, a necrotic torsed testis is managed by:
questions.exp: A necrotic testis requires orchidectomy. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: Orchidopexy for torsion uses:
questions.exp: The testis is fixed at three points with non-absorbable sutures. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Testicular Torsion
questions.q: After unilateral testicular torsion, the contralateral testis should undergo:
questions.exp: Prophylactic contralateral orchidopexy is performed because the predisposing anatomy may be bilateral. (Book p310)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: Epididymo-orchitis is an infection of the:
questions.exp: Epididymo-orchitis is infection of the epididymis plus testis. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The most common organism in epididymo-orchitis in a patient younger than 40 years is:
questions.exp: In patients under 40 years, Chlamydia is the commonest organism. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The most common organism in epididymo-orchitis in a patient older than 40 years is:
questions.exp: In patients over 40 years, E. coli is the commonest organism, secondary to UTI. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: A typical clinical feature of epididymo-orchitis is:
questions.exp: Epididymo-orchitis presents with acute scrotal pain and swelling. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The important differential diagnosis of acute epididymo-orchitis is:
questions.exp: Testicular torsion is the important differential diagnosis. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: Initial management of epididymo-orchitis includes:
opts: Antibiotics, scrotal support and pain killers
questions.exp: Management is antibiotics plus scrotal support and pain killers. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: A hydrocele is an accumulation of fluid in the:
questions.exp: Hydrocele is fluid accumulation in the tunica vaginalis. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The most common type of hydrocele is:
questions.exp: Vaginal hydrocele is the commonest type. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: A vaginal hydrocele consists of fluid accumulation:
questions.exp: Vaginal hydrocele is fluid only around the testis. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The commonest type of vaginal hydrocele is:
questions.exp: Primary vaginal hydrocele is the commonest type. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: Primary vaginal hydrocele is caused by:
questions.exp: Primary hydrocele is due to decreased absorption. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: Secondary vaginal hydrocele is caused by:
questions.exp: Secondary vaginal hydrocele is due to increased secretion. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The most common cause of secondary vaginal hydrocele listed is:
questions.exp: Secondary hydrocele is most commonly secondary to epididymo-orchitis; trauma and tumours are also listed. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: A primary hydrocele is usually:
opts: A tense swelling with the testis not separately palpable
A lax swelling with the testis clearly palpable
questions.exp: Primary hydrocele is tense and the testis is not separately palpable. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: A secondary hydrocele is usually:
opts: A lax swelling with the testis separately palpable
A tense swelling with no testis palpable
A solid mass in the renal angle
questions.exp: Secondary hydrocele is lax and the testis is separately palpable. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: A primary hydrocele usually contains:
opts: Air that gives a double bubble sign
questions.exp: Primary hydrocele contains clear fluid and is brilliantly transilluminant. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: A secondary hydrocele usually:
opts: Does not transilluminate because the fluid is turbid
questions.exp: Secondary hydrocele has turbid fluid and no transillumination. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The operation listed for a small hydrocele is:
questions.exp: Lord's plication is used for small hydroceles. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: Jaboulay's procedure consists of:
opts: Eversion and suturing of the sac
questions.exp: Jaboulay's procedure is eversion plus suturing of the hydrocele sac. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: An inguinoscrotal swelling in infantile hydrocele has which getting-above sign?
opts: Getting above the swelling is negative
Getting above the swelling is positive
It is positive only after exercise
questions.exp: In infantile hydrocele, an inguinoscrotal swelling cannot be got above. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
questions.q: The treatment of infantile hydrocele is:
opts: Excision of excess sac with eversion of the sac
questions.exp: Infantile hydrocele is treated by excision of excess sac and eversion of the sac. (Book p311)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Congenital hydrocele is associated with a:
questions.exp: Congenital hydrocele has a patent processus vaginalis. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: A patent processus vaginalis in congenital hydrocele communicates with the:
questions.exp: The patent processus vaginalis communicates with the peritoneal cavity. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Congenital hydrocele is associated with a:
questions.exp: The chapter depicts a hernial sac with congenital hydrocele. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: The treatment of congenital hydrocele is:
opts: Herniotomy, done by 2–3 years of age
Lord's plication at birth in every case
questions.exp: Congenital hydrocele is treated by herniotomy, done by 2–3 years of age. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Hydrocele of the cord presents as:
questions.exp: Hydrocele of the cord presents as swelling along the cord. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Symptomatic hydrocele of the cord is treated by:
questions.exp: Symptomatic hydrocele of the cord is treated by excision. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: A spermatocele is usually:
opts: Multiloculated like a bunch of grapes
questions.exp: Spermatocele is unilocular; an epididymal cyst is multiloculated. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: An epididymal cyst is characteristically:
opts: Multiloculated, like a bunch of grapes
questions.exp: An epididymal cyst is multiloculated and has a bunch-of-grapes appearance. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: A spermatocele involves the:
questions.exp: The spermatocele involves the epididymal head. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: An epididymal cyst represents:
questions.exp: An epididymal cyst is due to cystic degeneration of the epididymis. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: The fluid in a spermatocele is described as:
questions.exp: Spermatocele contains barley-coloured fluid. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: The fluid in an epididymal cyst is:
opts: Crystal clear and gives a Chinese-lantern transillumination pattern
questions.exp: Epididymal cyst contains crystal-clear fluid and transilluminates in a Chinese-lantern pattern. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Spermatocele contains:
questions.exp: Sperm are present in a spermatocele. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: The treatment of a symptomatic spermatocele is:
questions.exp: A symptomatic spermatocele is treated by excision, which may cause infertility. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Excision of a symptomatic spermatocele may cause:
questions.exp: Excision of a spermatocele may cause infertility. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: The treatment of a symptomatic epididymal cyst is:
questions.exp: A symptomatic epididymal cyst is treated by excision. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Scrotal sebaceous cysts are due to:
questions.exp: Scrotal sebaceous cysts are due to blocked hair follicle ducts. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: Scrotal sebaceous cysts are associated with:
opts: A very high risk of seminoma
An increased risk of renal-cell carcinoma
questions.exp: The chapter states that scrotal sebaceous cysts do not increase cancer risk. (Book p312)

questions.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
questions.q: The treatment of a symptomatic scrotal sebaceous cyst is:
questions.exp: Symptomatic scrotal sebaceous cysts are treated by excision. (Book p312)

units.title: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent
units.sec: Surgical Anatomy, Blood Supply and Descent · p307
units.guide: The testis develops in the retroperitoneal genital ridge and descends under the pull of the contractile gubernaculum, hormonal factors and differential abdominal-wall growth. Remember the transport map: epididymis to vas, rete testis to epididymis; the left testicular vein takes a long right-angled route to the left renal vein, while left and right testicular lymph drain first to para-aortic and interaortocaval groups respectively.

units.title: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management
units.sec: Undescended Testis: Pathophysiology, Workup and Management · p308
units.guide: An undescended testis is arrested on its normal route, usually in the inguinal canal, with the right side more often involved. It shrinks, injures Sertoli cells and spermatogenesis, raises intratubular germ-cell neoplasia and seminoma risk, and brings trauma, torsion, infertility and indirect hernia; use ultrasound for an inguinal testis and diagnostic laparoscopy for an intra-abdominal one. Wait for spontaneous descent only to five months, operate at 6–12 months, and follow the beta-hCG/laparoscopy and orchidopexy algorithms; distinguish ectopic from retractile testis.

units.title: Testicular Torsion
units.guide: Torsion is an acute surgical emergency in a young male: the bell-clapper anatomy, severe pain, high-riding transverse testis and painful Prehn sign point to absent Doppler flow. Salvage is best within six hours, so explore rather than delay; de-rotate and fix a viable testis, remove a necrotic one, use three-point non-absorbable fixation and fix the other side prophylactically.

units.title: Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
units.guide: Epididymo-orchitis infects both epididymis and testis: Chlamydia is common below 40 years and E. coli above 40 years, but torsion must be excluded. Hydrocele is fluid in the tunica vaginalis: primary is common, decreased absorption, tense, clear and brilliantly transilluminant; secondary is increased secretion, commonly from epididymo-orchitis, lax, separately palpable and turbid. Match the hydrocele operation to the lesion — Lord for small sacs, Jaboulay for eversion and suture, and excision plus eversion for infantile hydrocele.

units.title: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions
units.sec: Congenital Hydrocele and Miscellaneous Scrotal Conditions · p312
units.guide: Congenital hydrocele communicates through a patent processus vaginalis and is treated with age-appropriate herniotomy; cord hydrocele runs along the cord and is excised when symptomatic. A spermatocele is a unilocular barley-coloured, sperm-containing epididymal-head lesion, whereas an epididymal cyst is a multiloculated crystal-clear Chinese-lantern lesion. Both symptomatic lesions are excised, while scrotal sebaceous cysts arise from blocked hair-follicle ducts without increased cancer risk.
